reference_sql:
SELECT order_id, product_id, COUNT(*) AS n_lines
FROM order_lines
GROUP BY order_id, product_id, quantity, unit_price_eur, promo_id, line_discount_eur
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
alternatives:
WITH line_sets AS (  -- one row per set of matching lines
  SELECT order_id, product_id, COUNT(*) AS n_lines
  FROM order_lines
  GROUP BY order_id, product_id, quantity, unit_price_eur, promo_id, line_discount_eur
)
SELECT order_id, product_id, n_lines
FROM line_sets
WHERE n_lines > 1
SELECT order_id, product_id, COUNT(order_line_id) AS n_lines FROM order_lines GROUP BY order_id, product_id, quantity, unit_price_eur, promo_id, line_discount_eur HAVING COUNT(order_line_id) >= 2

other_way.tradeoff: A named step with WHERE on its count shows every set before the test, but HAVING tests the groups in one query.
